最近发现一个glog不错的替代品，loguru，

Directly use mkl

因为之前想要用dlopen使用blas库，但是这样使用blas库会造成OpenMP冲突，于是我们想直接链接blas库。

进而，我们不需要写一个兼容层，因为blas的接口大部分是一样的，小部分不一样的，比如gemm_batch和vsTanh可以使用mkl的接口，如果以后要兼容openblas的话，可以按照MKL的接口实现。

commit message:
Merge branch 'polish_cuda_cmake' into 'develop' (merge request !81)

polish cuda cmake
- 将`sm_35 sm_50 sm_52 sm_60 sm_61 sm_70`架构的二进制代码写入目标文件，这样可以使得运行时节省从ptx文件转为二进制文件的过程。
- 将`sm_70`的ptx文件写入目标文件，这样的话，得到的目标文件可以在更高的架构上运行。

这样做的好处是，代码可以在更多架构上运行，但是不好的地方是，可能会导致编译时间变长，并且编译得到的目标文件变大。

Note:理论上可以在Kepler、Maxwell、Pascal、Volta、Turing、Ampere架构上运行，但是目前只在Maxwell架构上测试过。


参考： https://arnon.dk/matching-sm-architectures-arch-and-gencode-for-various-nvidia-cards/

commit message:
- part of the precise timing definitions was moved to timing.c/h to be available always, as alternative to time(). In particular, it is used for precise measurement of total wall time for program execution. GetTime is replaced by GET_SYSTEM_TIME, DiffSec - by DiffSystemTime.
- minor fixes in precise timing of D-matrix initialization (several printfs were not accounted for, except in total time). Now the total time (for D-matrix init) exactly (within 1 in the last shown digit) equals the sum of the parts. Same is true for other parts of precise timing.
- removed "naive" transpose OpenCL kernels completely, since the cached one works well in all cases.
- rearranged first lines (definitions) in kernels arith2-4, so that they are ordered by arguments of get_global_id/size. This way it is easier to compare those definitions with the arguments of corresponding kernel invocations.
- fftw plans for D,R-matrix transforms (during initialization) are now also destroyed in OpenCL mode. fftw_cleanup calls added in the end of fftw usage (either in fftInitAfterD or in Free_FFT_Dmat).
- minor change in initialization of random generator in PlaceGranules() in make_particle.c. Should not change anything.
- a few cosmetic changes in somnec.c to remove compiler warnings with regards to definition of complex numbers (probably appeared in gcc 4.8).
- r1349 was incorporated (updated) into the code just before the commit. It merged well, so no problems are expected.

author: yurkin <yurkin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Major changes to the code due to switch to complex types of C99 (issue 70). All the code using complex numbers has been looked through, and in many cases it was significantly simplified. Many functions from cmplx.h (operating on complex scalars) has been removed, as they are no more used.
- E2_alldir is now used to store only the final result, while (intermediary) complex fields are stored in a new vector E_ad. This slightly increases required memory (proportional to number of angles), but improves clarity.
- removed restrict optimizations from cmplx.h, because the functions are inline anyway.
- added boolVector to memory.c/h (and a couple of minor corrections)
- arguments of CalcField in crosssec.c are now declared as 3-vectors.
- added test of gcc version in Makefile, '-pedantic' is used only for versions >= gcc (otherwise spurious warnings about complex numbers appear).
- MatVec in sparse mode was updated to use standard functions from linalg.c
- removed copying of scalar function arguments into registers for functions in linalg.c. That had some sense for double[2] arguments, but can be left to compiler to arguments that are passed by value.
- removed all '#pragma ivdep' in linalg.c, since now this information should be obvious to compiler anyway.
- version incremented to 1.3a1

MPI part:
- To have portable coupling with 'double complex', MPI_C_DOUBLE_COMPLEX is now used when available. However, it can be either unavailable, or not supported in reduction operations. Therefore, rather complicated logic has been added to parbas.h to detect different cases and take full advantage of the available features. Missing features are emulated by replacing 'double complex' with 'double[2]' as was before. But it is not perfectly portable.
- Similar issues were addressed for MPI_C_BOOL. The corresponding part of granule generator was changed to take full advantage of it.
- Accumulate() now operates in place and operates on any datatype. Corresponding buffers Egrid_buffer, Eplane_buffer, and E2alldir_buffer were removed (somewhat decreasing the memory footprint in MPI mode).

Quick tests of sequential and MPI parts showed marginal improvement of computational speed.
Both sequential and MPI parts (including sparse, without SSE3, counterparts) were thoroughly testes with tests/2exec.

Remaining issues: test and fix coupling with Fortran, C++, OpenCL parts, and sparse-SSE3. They seem to be working, but not perfectly portable.

commit message:

Error (wrong scaling) in backward FFTs with clAmdFft was corrected. Now it seems to be working fine for any grid size, even on GPU cards.
Fixes issue 144. 
And also a few of other minor changes to finalize this new feature:
- Using AMD clFFT is now the default one. Apple FFT can be used instead by using option CLFFT_APPLE in the Makefile. Hence, OpenCL version no more strictly relies on cpp sources, and is compatible with NO_CPP (hence, windows builds should be changed in the future).
- clAmdFft library name in ocl/Makefile was changed to clAmdFft.Runtime, since this seems to be the case on all OSs (at least for version 1.8).
- 'AMDFFT' in fft.c/h was changed to 'CLFFT_AMD' in line with newly created 'CLFFT_APPLE' and previously used 'FFT_TEMPERTON'.
- added comments about current limitation of current clAmdFft API for plan creation in comparison with fftw_guru.
- added initialization call to clAmdFftSetup().
- added debug output of clAmdFft (and FFTW) library versions. 
- minor changes in (legacy) FFT_TEMPERTON code to make more similar to existing ones.
- fftFit() was slightly reworked. 
- log in OpenCL mode now includes the used clFFT algorithm (AMD or APPLE)
- output of '-V' now includes version of found clAmdFft library (if relevant).

- USE_CLBLAS renamed into OCL_BLAS. There is little order in naming of such options currently. But the idea is that "use" is redundant (USE_SSE3 will probably be removed in the future), while OpenCL options should start with OCL (CLFFT_... are currently exceptions).
- ocl/Makefile now includes additional information about clAmdBlas. Makefile produces message about using option OCL_BLAS.
- Output of '-V' now gives the version of clAmdBlas (during compilation) and extra make option (OCL_BLAS). In full-debug mode ADDA also gives the version of clAmdBlas that is linked at runtime (during normal execution).
- slightly improved intitialization of complex scalars to remove compiler warnings.
- added error checks (CL_CH_ERR) to many ocl function calls.
- changed type of bufupload from cl_bool to bool.
- removed typecasts of local_nrows to size_t (already this type).
- additional buffer allocation (and release) in fft.c was changed to happen only for BiCG iterative solver.

Remaining issues:
- same limitations as with r1349.
- compilation problems on Windows (workarounds exist, will be addressed further).

Other changes:
- added NO_SVNREV to a list of valid options in Makefile and to output of '-V'. It was forgotten during r1231, hence this option has not been working through a command line to make. Also an information message is given during compilation.
- param.c now includes oclAmdFft.version.h instead of oclAmdFft.h (should be sufficient).

commit message:
Improvements to the near_field package.

1) Issue 123 describes the inconsistency between ADDA and near_field. ADDA's issue was corrected by r1008, but there still exist some non-trivial functionality in ADDA which can lead to weird shape files. near_field's issue (when working with weird shape files) can be partly alleviated by simple suggestion given by Fabio http://groups.google.com/group/adda-discuss/msg/a1110e72866576fd . 

However, the limitation of it is the assumption that center of the particle coincides (within shift of 0.5 dipoles) with the center of the computational domain. Moreover, two variable (rc{x,y,z} and ic{x,y,z}) are used to describe almost the same quantity, while difference between them is used as an indicator of parity of number of dipoles along the corresponding axes.

The correction sets rc equal to exact center of the computational domain, using both target (integer coordinates) and DipPol (real dipole coordinates). Thus rc is further directly used in e.g. calcbeam to get real coordinates of any point. ic was replaced by pc, which is double the coordinates of the particle center, i.e. the center of the _minimal_ box (with possibly odd sizes) enclosing the particle. Since this center is either integer or half-integer, pc is always integer, which is convenient for further use.

The new version of near_field should work with any shape files, even those not-completely-correct produced by older ADDA versions. This was checked on data provided at http://code.google.com/p/a-dda/issues/detail?id=123#c8 (with small modifications).

2) One of the ways to produce weird shape files, for which the above correction is necessary, is to run ADDA with "-shape read ... grid ..." where arguments to grid are larger than coordinates sizes given by the shape file. Thus a test case was added to RUNTESTS/readodd, which should not be passed by previous version of near_field.

3) All 'run...' scripts were improved by adding checking of ADDA errors. So now the test will not continue if ADDA fails. Also added 'clean' scripts to remove all files produced during runs.

Alternative way of handling cl sources was added (currently this applies only to oclkernels.cl). They are stringified during compile time, by transforming them in a C string that is put in a separate file. This file (.clstr) is then included in the C source as a static string. This way of handling cl sources is now the default one, but can be changed by define READ_CL_SOURCE_AT_RUNTIME in oclcore.c. commit message:
1) Compilation options (DEBUG, FFT_TEMPERTON, etc.) are now specified by variable OPTIONS instead of directly by definitions in the $(CFLAGS). $(OPTIONS) can be specified either in the Makefile (as before) or given by the environment or in the command line of make. The latter allows convenient ways to automate compilation with different options. Moreover, the list of words in $(OPTIONS) is checked against the predefined list of valid values. Information about compilation options is now given in a more convenient format.
2) Processing of $(OPTIONS) adds flags to new variable CDEFS to be completely independent of $(CFLAGS). Other definitions (like -DMPI) are now also passed to compiler by $(CDEFS).
3) Adding extra flags to $(CFLAGS) is now done not directly but through a new variable EXTRA_CFLAGS. The latter can also be specified outside of the Makefile.
4) Comments were added concerning the specification of $(OPTIONS), $(COMPILER), and $(EXTRA_CFLAGS) from the environment or the command line of make. Also possibility of overriding values of $(CFLAGS), $(FFLAGS), $(LDFLAGS), and $(LDLIBS) was mentioned (with proper caution).
5) mpi/Makefile now contains heuristics that searches for mpicc and use it as compiler if found. Otherwise $(CC) is used. This should remove the need to manually define $(MPICC) in this Makefile in most cases.

commit message:
A lot of improvements to sparse mode:
- Macro (flag) ADDA_SPARSE was shortened to SPARSE.
- Makefiles modified to produce info about SPARSE and USE_SSE3 and set up interaction (errors) with other options.
- Gather operations of sparse mode are now performed through AllGather(). For that it was modified to enable in-place operation, and a new MPI_Datatype mpi_int3 was introduced. Previously used functions and variables has been removed.
- In sparse mode local_nvoid_d0 and local_nvoid_d1 are now initialized in ParSetup(), while SetupLocalD() is not called at all.
- Memory optimizations: material_full and remnants of DipoleCoord_full are eliminated, 'position' is no more allocated but just points to a part of position_full.
- A lot of indexes in sparse_ops.h are now size_t instead of int. Among other changes, Fixes issue 159.
- Fixed initialization of mat_count in MakeParticle() in sparse mode. It was broken and led 
- Timings for init Dmatrix and FFT setup are no more shown in sparse mode.
- All command line options, not supported in sparse mode, are now explicitly removed during compilation (with appropriate modification of help texts). These includes: '-shape ...' (except read), '-init_field wkb', -granul, -save_geom, -sg_format, -store_grans.
- Removed error messages when using '-int ...' (except poi) in sparse mode. Now these options work fine, but relatively slow.
- Information about compile options SPARSE and USE_SSE3 (when used) has been added to output of option -V. Added information about sparse mode to log file (instead of information about FFT method).
- Added meaningful error message for default run of adda (without command line parameters) in sparse mode.
- A lot of formatting changes to make the sparse mode similar to the rest of the code.

Other changes:
- interaction.c/h now holds all the code related to calculation of Green's tensor. In particular, reading/freeing of table integrals was moved from calculator.c, and duplicating code to compute Green's tensor in fft.c was removed. 
An important change is that now functions, which compute Green's tensor do not test for zero argument. Hence, these test is now made in InitDmatrix().
- Intermediate vector DipoleCoord_tmp is no more used in make_particle.c. This somewhat decreases memory usage during prognosis. Overall, the code in MakeParticle() was significantly changed (a lot of moving parts around).
- oclcore.h is now always included, but is void if OPENCL is not specified. That is similar to other conditional headers like fft.h.
- Tests (tests/2exec) were modified to incorporate sparse mode (to compare two sparse mode versions or sparse mode vs. FFT mode). Corresponding tests are listed in separate file - suite_sparse, which is automatically used if appropriate flag is uncommented in comp2exec.  Added 2 new shape files and modified ellipsoid.geom. Improved behavior of diff_numeric.awk - before it was skipping differences, if the line was missing in the first file.
- A number of files (new or heavily modified) were formatted for a window width of 120 symbols.
- A number of minor syntax changes to remove warnings by Eclipse code analyzer. In particular, changed several empty statements from ";" to "{}", removed two unused functions, and hid several extern declarations in sparse mode.
- Fixed crashes when using command line options '-shape' and '-beam' without arguments. Now meaningful error messages are produced.
- version incremented to 1.2b2.

The updated code was tested to compile in different compilation modes (almost all possible combinations) and tested by tests/2exec/ against the version 1.1.

commit message:
Two major changes to makefiles:
- Debug level can be now one of three levels:
  1) default one (formerly release) - no debug symbols, no warnings, maximum optimization.
  2) DEBUG - turns on producing debug symbols (-g) and warnings and brings optimization down to O2 (to produce all possible warnings by the compiler).
  3) DEBUGFULL turns off optimization completely (for more accurate debugging symbols) and turns on additional diagnostic messages in the source code (formerly DEBUG).
Debugging seems to be working in a bundle Eclipse-MinGW-gdb. Fixes issue 65.

- Compilation options are now saved to .lastopts. If new options are different from the last ones (as unordered sets of words), then complete recompilation is performed. This allows safe and efficient passing compilation options to makefiles through the command line.

Other changes in the source files: 
- DEBUG changed to DEBUGFULL
- several minor edits to remove 'uninitialized' and 'unused' warnings

commit message:
Iterative solvers were significantly refactored by moving all common parts to the main calling function (IterativeSolver). Most of the constants were gathered into one structure array (params). The functions, implementing the iterative solvers, now consist of three independent parts - phases (chosen by the input variable) with only static local variables shared between them (seems like a C++ object). Checkpoint data structure was slightly changed - instead of enum variable, denoting the iterative method, int variable, denoting its index, is now used. In particular, this makes current version incompatible with all previous versions in terms of reading checkpoints. Most of this should not influence the results, except the compiler-optimization-related uncertainties. But one significant line from the BiCGstab code was removed (inside intermediate test for convergence). It seems that it was there by mistake, although it didn't influenced the results.

Added comments throughout the code on how to add a new iterative solver. A lot of other related comments were also added. 

Functions for parsing specific command line parameters are now all declared as static.

author: yurkin@gmail.com <yurkin@gmail.com@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
Major changes to the code due to switch to complex types of C99 (issue 70). All the code using complex numbers has been looked through, and in many cases it was significantly simplified. Many functions from cmplx.h (operating on complex scalars) has been removed, as they are no more used.
- E2_alldir is now used to store only the final result, while (intermediary) complex fields are stored in a new vector E_ad. This slightly increases required memory (proportional to number of angles), but improves clarity.
- removed restrict optimizations from cmplx.h, because the functions are inline anyway.
- added boolVector to memory.c/h (and a couple of minor corrections)
- arguments of CalcField in crosssec.c are now declared as 3-vectors.
- added test of gcc version in Makefile, '-pedantic' is used only for versions >= gcc (otherwise spurious warnings about complex numbers appear).
- MatVec in sparse mode was updated to use standard functions from linalg.c
- removed copying of scalar function arguments into registers for functions in linalg.c. That had some sense for double[2] arguments, but can be left to compiler to arguments that are passed by value.
- removed all '#pragma ivdep' in linalg.c, since now this information should be obvious to compiler anyway.
- version incremented to 1.3a1

MPI part:
- To have portable coupling with 'double complex', MPI_C_DOUBLE_COMPLEX is now used when available. However, it can be either unavailable, or not supported in reduction operations. Therefore, rather complicated logic has been added to parbas.h to detect different cases and take full advantage of the available features. Missing features are emulated by replacing 'double complex' with 'double[2]' as was before. But it is not perfectly portable.
- Similar issues were addressed for MPI_C_BOOL. The corresponding part of granule generator was changed to take full advantage of it.
- Accumulate() now operates in place and operates on any datatype. Corresponding buffers Egrid_buffer, Eplane_buffer, and E2alldir_buffer were removed (somewhat decreasing the memory footprint in MPI mode).

Quick tests of sequential and MPI parts showed marginal improvement of computational speed.
Both sequential and MPI parts (including sparse, without SSE3, counterparts) were thoroughly testes with tests/2exec.

Remaining issues: test and fix coupling with Fortran, C++, OpenCL parts, and sparse-SSE3. They seem to be working, but not perfectly portable.

It is recommended to use the default 'dr' for all production runs.
  A new global variables chi_inv was added, which is calculated together with cc and cc_sqrt. It simplifies the code for internal field saving and calculation of Cabs. New global variable dipvol saves a few lines by avoiding unnecessary repetition. Version was incremented to 0.79b3.

Continuation of changes along r1204:
- qvec and qmunu are used everywhere, replacing in some parts qx-qz, and qxx-qzz.
- CalcInterParams was split into two parts to be called before and after the IGT external routines.

- expval returned by CalcInterTerm_core is now exp(ikR)/R^3
- removed several redundant variables in CalcInterTerm_fcd and CalcInterTerm_fcd_st
- static declaration of variables removed in interaction.c and sparse_ops.h. While this may cause a minor performance decrease, it adds thread-safety. The latter is important for these functions, if we will implement OpenMP parallelization.
- 'result' in function arguments is now explicitly specified as [static restrict 6] in interaction.c/h
- removed several includes of function.h 
- also added several comment statements about thread safety.

The new code passed the tests in tests/2exec and produced similar timings to r1204 (<1% difference) both with and without SSE3. However, these timings for SSE3 versions were about 4% slower than that of r1200. The reason for that is unknown.

author: yurkin <yurkin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Implementation of point-dipole incident field (issue 149). Should work both for free space and in the presence of surface (dipole should be above the surface). Controlled by new beam type: '-beam dipole <x> <y> <z>', dipole is assumed to have unity amplitude with direction, given by '-prop ...' command line option (e_z by default).

To do this the logic in interaction.c/h was significantly modified. Now two types of functions are defined (visible outside) for both direct and reflected interaction, accepting either integers (in units of d, used for filling interaction matrix) or real values (in um, useful for other applications, such as incident dipole field or nearfields). Thus the whole existing machinery of interaction.c/h (all formulations, numerical routines, etc.) can easily be accessed from other parts of the code.
- internally, those functions are usually wrappers which reuse most of the code by calling inline functions.
- some of the interaction formulations (igt_so and so) are incompatible with arbitrary real arguments, since they are tightly linked to existing tables. If used they produce a careful exception (new flag InteractionRealArgs added for that).
- computing reflected Green's tensor (based on Sommerfeld integrals) was split into modules, including the tabulation. Now further optimization efforts can be directed precisely.

Still a lot to do - to test, integrate (add exceptions) to other parts of ADDA, add enhancement rates (radiative and non-radiative) to the output.

Other (related) changes:
- a number of exceptions with respect to combination of different beam types, -prop, and -surf were moved from VariablesInterconnect to InitBeam. Now they are more accurate.
- beam info for Gaussian beam was made more uniform. For centered beams, "Center is in the origin" was changed to "Center position: (0,0,0)".
- new functions cSymMatrVecReal and cReflMatrVecReal in cmplx.h
- version incremented to 1.3b2.
- test suites in tests/2exec/ were updated to include new features.

commit message:
This is a major change to the code, which contains several interwoven developments.

1) New option '-beam read <filenameY> [<filenameX>]' has been added to allow reading of incident beam from file. The same format as for '-store_beam'. Only a few consistency checks are done, so this is currently mostly left to the user (to supply exactly the same order of lines as in output file for the same geometry). It should be fully operational in MPI mode.

2) Significant changes to MPI functions. MPI_SIZE_T type has been added to parbas.h. Two new compound types were created - mpi_double3 and mpi_dcomplex3, construction of mpi_dcomplex was simplified. 'enum var_type' has been expanded to include all these compound types, and function MPIVarType() was added for automatic determination of the corresponding MPI datatype. All routines that work with different datatypes now handle them in a simpler uniform way. When reduce operation is performed, compound datatypes are automatically replaced by basic ones. Global variables local_nvoid_d0 and local_nvoid_d1 has been introduced, which simplify collective file operations. AllGather() was rewritten to work with any non-uniform distribution of non-void dipoles among processors. Now it also includes auxilliary function InitDispls().

3) Radiation forces has been significantly improved. Before they were not working in parallel mode at all. Now they work the same as in sequential mode, except for incomplete writing of VisFrp file.

4) Other stuff, mainly refactoring the code a little bit. 

Functions SkipFullLine(), FgetsError(), SkipNLines(), and SkipComments has been moved from make_particle.c to io.c, since they are now used for reading beam files as well.

New options for narg element of suboptions - FNAME_ARG_2 and FNAME_ARG_1_2. Auxilliary functions in param.c were adjusted. Function  ScanFnamesError() was added TestNarg() and TestNarg_sub were combined into one, fixind a minor bug on the way. Also ScanfDoubleError() was renamed to ScanDoubleError(), ScanfIntError() to ScanIntError(). TestStrLength() evolved into ScanStrError().

Type of nvoid_Ndip has been changed from double to size_t, since using more than 4 Gdipoles on a cluster of 32-bit machines is not practical anyway. Rigorous error checks has been implemented. The same applies to types of local_nvoid_d0 and local_nvoid_d1, and nd in PlaceGranules().

nlocalRows has been renamed to local_nRows for uniformity with other local_* variables. This affects quite a lot of source files.

version incremented to 1.1b2. Extensive tests were performed against 1.0 version using tests/2exec.

author: yurkin <yurkin@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
A separate branch - proof-of-principle implementation of the weighted discretization. It works only for spheres without anisotropy. Includes the following features (they may be useful in other applications as well)
1) Continuous refractive index and polarizability (increases memory requirements a little bit).
2) Simplest version of weighted discretization by using effective refractive index, determined by the occupied volume fraction of the dipole.
3) Routine to approximately determine the volume of intersection of the cube with the sphere. It starts with replacing a sphere with a tangent plane, which error is order of d/R (d - dipole size, R - radius of curvature). This simple approximation can be easily generalized to other shapes. Additionally, sphere-specific formulae are derived for accurate correction of order d/R, so the final inaccuracy is of order (d/R)^2. However, the latter corrections are not so straightforward to generalize.
4) Routine AbsOutProd in cmplx.h for absolute value of the outer product of two vectors.

Limited tests of this implementation were performed. The total volume of all dipoles (judged by the volume-equivalent radius) is very close to the true value. Moreover, the difference (error) goes to zero with order of d/R between 3 and 4 (which is as it should).

The accuracy of Cext is better than with standard discretization, but approximately the same as when using the simple volume correction of the whole dipole set.

To conclude, a lot of further development and research is required to understand the benefits of using weighting discretization. In particular, the weighting by Piller and Martin need to be implemented.

- Code for FFTX,Y,Z and TransposeY,Z in matvec.c (for OpenCL) was moved into the corresponding functions in fft.c.

- malloc and free calls in fft.c and oclcore.c were replaced by wrappers from memory.c/h.
- clReleaseKernel calls were added for clConj and clinprod to oclunload() in oclcore.c.

- Releasing OpenCL buffers was moved from oclunload() in oclcore.c to Free_FFT_Dmat() in fft.c.
- Makefiles were changed to incorporate ocl and cpp sources in a natural way (absolutely analogously to what was before for mpi and fort respectively).
- MAX_LINE in const.h was changed from 50 to 100.
- svn:ignore property of ocl/ was set appropriately.
- definition of many variables in MatVec(...) was moved under "#ifndef OPENCL" to remove not-used warnings.

Should be enough. 2) error handling was partly replaced by checkErr, now it will stop after the first error (except inside the loop). Checking of final error was moved into the function itself, so GetDevice() returns nothing now. 3) arguments were replaced by the variables defined for whole oclcore.c. devtype was made a local variable of GetDevice(). 4) printf was added to indicate which platform was found.

author: yurkin <yurkin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Finally, a working implementation of particle near surface in FFT mode.
- additional required memory was described in comments in calculator.c
- definition of ZsumShift is now different for sparse and FFT modes in parallel (relative to the local or global bottom dipoles respectively). Related difference is in definition of local_Nz_Rm (used for Sommerfeld table and, in FFT mode, for filling Rmatrix).
- Sommerfeld table is now not calculated during prognosis, but corresponding memory is properly accounted for.
- Current implementation requires additional forward fftY and fftZ at each iteration (but see issue 177).
- BlockTranspose_Dm in comm.c was renamed into BlockTranspose_DRm, since it works both for D- and Rmatrix.
- existing functions to index Dmatrix has been slightly changed to not use DsizeYZ and use y>=DsizeY instead of y>smallY.
- functions and plans, not specific to Dmatrix were renamed (Y and Z forward transforms), now they have 'slice' in their names.
- transposeYZ_Dm was changed to transpose (a general function), and transposeYZ is now just a wrapper around the latter.
- version incremented to 1.3b1.

Main computational bottleneck is computation of the table of Sommerfeld integrals. Currently it is approximately equivalent to 200 iterations (issue 176). So should not be a problem for applications with a larger number of iterations.

New implementation was extensively tested against previous sparse version. Still, quantitative comparison with published literature data is required. Remaining limitation is that it doesn't work in OpenCL mode (see issue 101 for details, explicit exception was added to param.c).

Changes to timing:
- added time for 'init interaction' (significant when Sommerfeld table is calculated).
- Time for 'init Dmatrix' now may include the time for initialization of Rmatrix (doesn't include time for Sommerfeld table).
- Precise timing for Dmatrix now includes a separate line for initialization of Rmatrix (without details)

Other:
- scattering at exactly 90 degrees (along surface) for non-trivial surfaces is now handled by a special case to produce exact 0. This makes the output consistent, avoiding large integration errors for -phi_integr or alldir.
- added explicit exception to forbid combination of -no_reduced_fft and -iter cgnr in MPI FFT mode (issue 174).

Tests in tests/2exec/ have been significantly improved
- added SURF_EXT flag, which allows running a large suite of tests, adding '-surf ...' option to each of them.
- added a number of ignores, which are always active (decreases false-positives)
- added a couple of macros in suite files (NOMPI and NOMPISEQ), which indicates that the line should be skipped for a specific comparison modes.
- added a number of tests to the default suite: '-surf ...', '-int_surf', -scat_plane, '-shape read ... -grid ...', '-no_reduced_fft -iter cgnr' (see above)

author: yurkin@gmail.com <yurkin@gmail.com@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
- Calculation of scattering into the substrate was rewritten, using the reciprocity principle. In particular, the near-field propagation direction nN can now be complex. but the far-field wave is now always homogeneous. Fixes issue 184. Now Cext=Csca for dielectric substrate with good accuracy (depends on number of angles to integrate Csca, which is generally larger than for free-space case due to discontinuity at theta=90 deg).
- Scattered field (amplitude) is normalized by k_sca (which is msub times larger, when scattering into the substrate).
- Changed the normalization of the incident beam (when coming from the substrate). Now it has unity amplitude, so that the amplitude matrix directly corresponds to the incident field. New global variable inc_scale=1/Re(minc) is initialized in GenerateB.c (minc is the refractive index of the medium, where the incident beam comes from).
- Muller matrix definition is updated to correspond to ratios of irradiances, so ComputeMuellerMatrix() now includes a factor Re(m_sca)/Re(m_inc) (when needed) and requires theta as additional argument. 
- 'E2_alldir' now stores values scaled with Re(1/msca). This is proportional to the Poynting vector and is more convenient for calculation of Csca and related quantities.
- Cross sections (Cext, Cabs, Csca) and asymmetry vector (g*Csca) are normalized by incoming irradiance, so they now include a factor of inc_scale. Generalization of g to the surface case is straightforward, but loses physical sense (scattered momentum).
- New definition for fields and other computed quantities are given in the manual (will be committed later).
- TestBelowDeg() was added in cmplx.h. imExp_arr() now accepts complex arguments.

Two minor bugs were fixed:
- Detection of symmetry of theta angle (range pi or 2*pi) is improved to correctly account for both -yz and -scat_plane.
- In calculation of scattering plane for SCAT_GRID in MuellerMatrix() theta was used without conversion to radians. But this should not have affected any results.

author: yurkin@gmail.com <yurkin@gmail.com@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
Implemented calculation of reflected Green's tensor, approximated by a single image dipole, and its use in simulations in sparse (non-FFT) mode. The important detail is that now the sum in matrix-vector product includes the self-interaction (only the surface-reflected part). Another detail is that the 3x3 reflected Green's tensor have unusual symmetry, but the total 3Nx3N matrix is still complex-symmetric.

Simulation results for a sphere above a perfectly conducting surface (imitated by surface with m=100) agree qualitatively with the analytical calculations in B.R. Johnson, “Light scattering from a spherical particle on a conducting plane: I. Normal incidence,” J. Opt. Soc. Am. A 9, 1341–1351 (1992). I've tried grids 4,8,16,32 and the resulting phase function does seem to converge to the Fig.7 from the paper.

Fixed bug, introduced in recent implementation of -scat_plane. The latter was not working properly in case of rotational symmetry (when only one incident polarization was simulated) both for fixed and random orientation. Now, -scat_plane (instead of -yz) doesn't change the results for rotationally-symmetric particles with default incident direction. Also, an explicit test was introduced, which forbids enforcing symmetry in combination with -scat_plane and incident propagation not along the z-axis.

Added one line (for reverse propagation) in test suites in tests/2exec/

author: yurkin <yurkin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Implemented calculation of the scattered fields in the presence of surface (scattering directions both above and below). It is located in a separate function CalcFieldSurf(). There are, however, certain limitations for scattering below the surface when refractive index of the substrate is complex (not real). The main problem is that the scattered wave in such medium is inhomogeneous and p-polarization is determined by a complex unit vector (such that e.e=1). This complication is not yet accounted for in the main part of the code (that would be very complicated, especially in the case of some nontrivial scattering planes). So the calculated field itself is correct but it is then processed incorrectly further on (though correctness very much depends on a particular definition).

Also during calculation of Csca and g*Csca multipliers Re(msub) and Re(msub)^2 were added to |E|^2 for directions below the substrate. Thus those formula correspond to the total energy and momentum carried away by the scattered field for real msub. For complex msub it is still unclear, what should be the proper formulae (see comments in the code). Also the total momentum doesn't determine the total force even for non-absorbing substrate, since the substrate also absorbs momentum through reflection/refraction.

As a test, I've studied the convergence of Csca to the free-space result when msub->1. The difference in Csca seems to be O(sqrt(m-1)), but very large Jmax in integration over theta is required for proper analysis (up to 15-20). The latter is due to very sharp dependence of scattered intensity for theta near 90 degrees.

Other things:
- added functions vInit, cvInit, and vAlongZ to cmplx.h. The latter was moved from param.c
- function AsymParm() marked as unused.
- code in InitBeam() was slightly changed for surface, not to lose accuracy for near-z propagation.
- updsvnrev.sh was rewritten to avoid bashisms, so that it can be run under any shell (issue 172)

commit message:
Iterative solvers were significantly refactored by moving all common parts to the main calling function (IterativeSolver). Most of the constants were gathered into one structure array (params). The functions, implementing the iterative solvers, now consist of three independent parts - phases (chosen by the input variable) with only static local variables shared between them (seems like a C++ object). Checkpoint data structure was slightly changed - instead of enum variable, denoting the iterative method, int variable, denoting its index, is now used. In particular, this makes current version incompatible with all previous versions in terms of reading checkpoints. Most of this should not influence the results, except the compiler-optimization-related uncertainties. But one significant line from the BiCGstab code was removed (inside intermediate test for convergence). It seems that it was there by mistake, although it didn't influenced the results.

Added comments throughout the code on how to add a new iterative solver. A lot of other related comments were also added. 

Functions for parsing specific command line parameters are now all declared as static.

commit message:
Continuation of changes along r1204:
- qvec and qmunu are used everywhere, replacing in some parts qx-qz, and qxx-qzz.
- CalcInterParams was split into two parts to be called before and after the IGT external routines.
- added function OuterSym to cmplx.h - used in CalcInterParams2
- logic inside both versions of CalcInterTerm_core was streamlined by using two macros for diagonal and non-diagonal terms
- expval returned by CalcInterTerm_core is now exp(ikR)/R^3
- removed several redundant variables in CalcInterTerm_fcd and CalcInterTerm_fcd_st
- static declaration of variables removed in interaction.c and sparse_ops.h. While this may cause a minor performance decrease, it adds thread-safety. The latter is important for these functions, if we will implement OpenMP parallelization.
- 'result' in function arguments is now explicitly specified as [static restrict 6] in interaction.c/h
- removed several includes of function.h 
- also added several comment statements about thread safety.

The new code passed the tests in tests/2exec and produced similar timings to r1204 (<1% difference) both with and without SSE3. However, these timings for SSE3 versions were about 4% slower than that of r1200. The reason for that is unknown.

commit message:
Improvements of ocl version:
- added testing of OpenCL version during compilation of both main ADDA source and of OpenCL kernels (the latter at runtime of ADDA). Currently, the test is against version 1.0, which should never fail. But it can be easily updated in the future to a nontrivial case, if needed.
- support for double precision is now tested by analyzing supported device extensions before building the OpenCL kernels, resulting in more meaningful error messages. Moreover, cl_amd_fp64 is not used for all AMD GPUs, but only for those that do not support more general cl_khr_fp64 (latest AMD GPUs do support it).
- added "-cl-fast-relaxed-math" to build options of OpenCL kernels, since it is similar to -ffast-math, which has been used for compilation of the main ADDA source for a long time. However, the performance gain was not tested on GPUs.
- added minimalistic implementation of variable-length strings to oclcore.c - struct string and functions StrInit() and StrCatSpace(). It is used to combine build options for OpenCL source.
- when extracting build errors (CL_PROGRAM_BUILD_LOG) buffer is now allocated to incorporate the complete log. But this doesn't help a lot, since it anyway may be truncated by the OpenCL implementation (at something like 4kB or 8kB).
- added call to clUnloadCompiler() to the end of oclinit() - kind of cleaner.
- added a few degugging messages - D(...).

A related change in memory.c/h and make_particle.c: macro REALLOC_DVECTOR was changed to REALLOC_VECTOR, which accepts additional argument 'type' similar to MALLOC_VECTOR. Currently type can be char or double, but others can be easily needed when the need arise.

commit message:
Improvements and bug fixes of the ocl version:
- In many places in the code size_t arguments were passed to kernels as cl_long, which caused complete failure of 32-bit version. This was not realized before due to lack of 32-bit system with modern GPU. Now corresponding type, named in_sizet (equal to either cl_uint or cl_ulong) is chosen during ADDA compilation, and is further passed to compiler of ocl sources.
- optimized (cached) transpose kernels are not applicable to small problem sizes. That's why adda_ocl failed for box size<=4 (gridY<16 or gridZ<16). This is fixed by implementing fallback to non-cached kernel for small problems.
- indexing of cc_sqrt in kernels was wrong, causing adda_ocl to produce wrong results for inhomogeneous scatterers (e.g. coated). It was fixed.
- ndcomp is now cl_char instead of cl_long.
- mat (private variable) in kernels is now uchar instead of char.
- syntax of kernel transposeo was changed to be consistent with the rest of the code.

tests/2exec/comp2exec was updated, adding several ignores for ocl_seq mode. Current version of ADDA passes this test both on 32-bit and 64-bit Windows. There are only couple of trivial diffs: for -store_granul and -V. This can be considered a major milestone in development of adda_ocl.

commit message:
This is a major change to the code, which contains several interwoven developments.

1) New option '-beam read <filenameY> [<filenameX>]' has been added to allow reading of incident beam from file. The same format as for '-store_beam'. Only a few consistency checks are done, so this is currently mostly left to the user (to supply exactly the same order of lines as in output file for the same geometry). It should be fully operational in MPI mode.

2) Significant changes to MPI functions. MPI_SIZE_T type has been added to parbas.h. Two new compound types were created - mpi_double3 and mpi_dcomplex3, construction of mpi_dcomplex was simplified. 'enum var_type' has been expanded to include all these compound types, and function MPIVarType() was added for automatic determination of the corresponding MPI datatype. All routines that work with different datatypes now handle them in a simpler uniform way. When reduce operation is performed, compound datatypes are automatically replaced by basic ones. Global variables local_nvoid_d0 and local_nvoid_d1 has been introduced, which simplify collective file operations. AllGather() was rewritten to work with any non-uniform distribution of non-void dipoles among processors. Now it also includes auxilliary function InitDispls().

3) Radiation forces has been significantly improved. Before they were not working in parallel mode at all. Now they work the same as in sequential mode, except for incomplete writing of VisFrp file.

4) Other stuff, mainly refactoring the code a little bit. 

Functions SkipFullLine(), FgetsError(), SkipNLines(), and SkipComments has been moved from make_particle.c to io.c, since they are now used for reading beam files as well.

New options for narg element of suboptions - FNAME_ARG_2 and FNAME_ARG_1_2. Auxilliary functions in param.c were adjusted. Function  ScanFnamesError() was added TestNarg() and TestNarg_sub were combined into one, fixind a minor bug on the way. Also ScanfDoubleError() was renamed to ScanDoubleError(), ScanfIntError() to ScanIntError(). TestStrLength() evolved into ScanStrError().

Type of nvoid_Ndip has been changed from double to size_t, since using more than 4 Gdipoles on a cluster of 32-bit machines is not practical anyway. Rigorous error checks has been implemented. The same applies to types of local_nvoid_d0 and local_nvoid_d1, and nd in PlaceGranules().

nlocalRows has been renamed to local_nRows for uniformity with other local_* variables. This affects quite a lot of source files.

author: yurkin <yurkin@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
1) Compilation options (DEBUG, FFT_TEMPERTON, etc.) are now specified by variable OPTIONS instead of directly by definitions in the $(CFLAGS). $(OPTIONS) can be specified either in the Makefile (as before) or given by the environment or in the command line of make. The latter allows convenient ways to automate compilation with different options. Moreover, the list of words in $(OPTIONS) is checked against the predefined list of valid values. Information about compilation options is now given in a more convenient format.
2) Processing of $(OPTIONS) adds flags to new variable CDEFS to be completely independent of $(CFLAGS). Other definitions (like -DMPI) are now also passed to compiler by $(CDEFS).
3) Adding extra flags to $(CFLAGS) is now done not directly but through a new variable EXTRA_CFLAGS. The latter can also be specified outside of the Makefile.
4) Comments were added concerning the specification of $(OPTIONS), $(COMPILER), and $(EXTRA_CFLAGS) from the environment or the command line of make. Also possibility of overriding values of $(CFLAGS), $(FFLAGS), $(LDFLAGS), and $(LDLIBS) was mentioned (with proper caution).
5) mpi/Makefile now contains heuristics that searches for mpicc and use it as compiler if found. Otherwise $(CC) is used. This should remove the need to manually define $(MPICC) in this Makefile in most cases.

commit message:
A number of improvements related to OpenCL BLAS in iterative solver (after r1349).
- USE_CLBLAS renamed into OCL_BLAS. There is little order in naming of such options currently. But the idea is that "use" is redundant (USE_SSE3 will probably be removed in the future), while OpenCL options should start with OCL (CLFFT_... are currently exceptions).
- ocl/Makefile now includes additional information about clAmdBlas. Makefile produces message about using option OCL_BLAS.
- Output of '-V' now gives the version of clAmdBlas (during compilation) and extra make option (OCL_BLAS). In full-debug mode ADDA also gives the version of clAmdBlas that is linked at runtime (during normal execution).
- slightly improved intitialization of complex scalars to remove compiler warnings.
- added error checks (CL_CH_ERR) to many ocl function calls.
- changed type of bufupload from cl_bool to bool.
- removed typecasts of local_nrows to size_t (already this type).
- additional buffer allocation (and release) in fft.c was changed to happen only for BiCG iterative solver.

Remaining issues:
- same limitations as with r1349.
- compilation problems on Windows (workarounds exist, will be addressed further).

Other changes:
- added NO_SVNREV to a list of valid options in Makefile and to output of '-V'. It was forgotten during r1231, hence this option has not been working through a command line to make. Also an information message is given during compilation.
- param.c now includes oclAmdFft.version.h instead of oclAmdFft.h (should be sufficient).

commit message:
'-int igt_so' was implemented. That is Integrated Green's tensor computed approximately using series expansion in kd up to second order. It reuses tabulated integrals and part of the code of SO. Basically, it is the same as SO, but with removed part of the code that depends on m. So 'igt_so' it is almost as fast as the default 'poi' and almost as accurate as 'igt' (and slightly more accurate than, say, 'igt 3'. Fixes issue 84.

CalcInterTerm is slightly optimized. The significant change is that SO formulation do not breaks when table size is not enough, but uses 'medium' formula instead of 'close' one. The same algorithm works for newly implemented 'igt_so'. Also debugging code to print values of G was added.

author: yurkin@gmail.com <yurkin@gmail.com@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
- Many if-else-if sequences in the code were changed to switch. Apart from generally better readability of the code, this has several practical advantages. First, when testing enum variable (most of the tests in current code) compiler can test for completeness (e.g. that all possible enum cases are explicitly treated). Second, this can lead to significant speed increase (especially, inside loops. In particular, the loop inside MakeParticle() is now up to 20% faster (depending on a particular shape).
- The code for CalcField and SaveGeometry, has been simplified by moving conditions (if and switch) inside the loops (instead of code duplication that was used before). For CalcField that may incur a small overhead (from 0% to 5% depending on tests), but I think that the clarity is worth it. 
- macros INTERACT_DIAG(I) and INTERACT_NONDIAG(I) in interaction.c and JAGGED_BOX in param.c has been improved (put inside {}), so that they are syntaxly equivalent to functions.
- Fixed minor bug in tests/2exec/diff_numeric.awk (introduced by r1203 (some error messages were duplicated).
- Changes were tested with tests/2exec/comp2exec

Overall style for the switch is the following:
- case commands generally start on the next line (following case label) are finalized by 'break;' (on a separate line)
- but short commands can be put on the same line as case label (together with break if required)
- all cases (except empty fall-through ones) should end with break (or return) or an explicit comment like '// no break'. The latter is especially relevant for calls of no-return functions, like LogError.

author: yurkin <yurkin@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
A separate branch - proof-of-principle implementation of the weighted discretization. It works only for spheres without anisotropy. Includes the following features (they may be useful in other applications as well)
1) Continuous refractive index and polarizability (increases memory requirements a little bit).
2) Simplest version of weighted discretization by using effective refractive index, determined by the occupied volume fraction of the dipole.
3) Routine to approximately determine the volume of intersection of the cube with the sphere. It starts with replacing a sphere with a tangent plane, which error is order of d/R (d - dipole size, R - radius of curvature). This simple approximation can be easily generalized to other shapes. Additionally, sphere-specific formulae are derived for accurate correction of order d/R, so the final inaccuracy is of order (d/R)^2. However, the latter corrections are not so straightforward to generalize.
4) Routine AbsOutProd in cmplx.h for absolute value of the outer product of two vectors.

Limited tests of this implementation were performed. The total volume of all dipoles (judged by the volume-equivalent radius) is very close to the true value. Moreover, the difference (error) goes to zero with order of d/R between 3 and 4 (which is as it should).

The accuracy of Cext is better than with standard discretization, but approximately the same as when using the simple volume correction of the whole dipole set.

To conclude, a lot of further development and research is required to understand the benefits of using weighting discretization. In particular, the weighting by Piller and Martin need to be implemented.

author: yurkin <yurkin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Implemented calculations of decay-rate enhancement for point-dipole incident beam. Total part is calculated with the help of a new function DecayCross() in crosssec.c/h (similar to Cext), non-radiative part - by normalizing Cabs. In case of surface, all parts of decay-rate enhancement (total, rad, nonrad) are normalized to that in free space, but additionally enhancement due to surface alone is shown.

Still, it is not clear whether the non-radiative part should be adjusted to account for absorption in the substrate (when it is absorbing).

Also, incident polarizations (Y and X) are not shown in the log for point-dipole incident beam. This is a bit problematic for standard LDR polarizability, since its factor S depends on both prop and incPol. But it probably makes little sense to use LDR polarizability for such incident field anyway (recommendation should be added to the manual).

One test was run for dipole near a sphere was run and matched exactly to first row of Table 1 in S. D'Agostino, F. Della Sala, and L.C. Andreani, “Dipole-excited surface plasmons in metallic nanoparticles: Engineering decay dynamics within the discrete-dipole approximation,” Phys. Rev. B 87, 205413 (2013). However, a few hacks were used to exactly match the simulation conditions (based on raw data provided by Stefania D'Agostino.

commit message:
Several improvements to the ocl version:
- error handling was improved. Now it works through a function PrintCLErr with macro and inline wrappers, while the error output itself is produced by LogError (hence duplicated in logfile additionally to stdout). The typed-in name of the error was in most places replaced by automatically generated position in the source. Apart from shortening the code, it has a benefit that for normal execution no additional function calls is needed (since the test of error status is performed by inline wrapper). So error test can be included in call of any ocl function without worrying about performance.
- calls of oclinit and oclunload were moved from ADDAmain.c to calculator.c.
- info about found OpenCL device is now duplicated into log.
- removed redundant comments in function calls, which probably originated from some OCL samples.
- error output during building of OpenCL kernels is now a bit more detailed.

Several improvements to makefiles:
- the code to automatically generate dependencies in common.mk was improved. The compilation now stops immediately if compiler returns an error while scanning for dependencies.
- added NO_CPP option to Makefile similarly to NO_FORTRAN, together with consistency checks in the source files. For now this option has little sense, but may find some use in the future.
- added OCL_READ_SOURCE_RUNTIME option to Makefile, which is a renamed version of READ_CL_SOURCE_AT_RUNTIME from oclcore.c.

Commented definition of FFT_TEMPERTON was removed from fft.h, since it can't be used by itself anyway. It also requires inclusion of Fortran file into the compilation cycle, which is better handled on the Makefile side.

Minor changes in io.h and vars.c.

author: yurkin@gmail.com <yurkin@gmail.com@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
Implementation of point-dipole incident field (issue 149). Should work both for free space and in the presence of surface (dipole should be above the surface). Controlled by new beam type: '-beam dipole <x> <y> <z>', dipole is assumed to have unity amplitude with direction, given by '-prop ...' command line option (e_z by default).

To do this the logic in interaction.c/h was significantly modified. Now two types of functions are defined (visible outside) for both direct and reflected interaction, accepting either integers (in units of d, used for filling interaction matrix) or real values (in um, useful for other applications, such as incident dipole field or nearfields). Thus the whole existing machinery of interaction.c/h (all formulations, numerical routines, etc.) can easily be accessed from other parts of the code.
- internally, those functions are usually wrappers which reuse most of the code by calling inline functions.
- some of the interaction formulations (igt_so and so) are incompatible with arbitrary real arguments, since they are tightly linked to existing tables. If used they produce a careful exception (new flag InteractionRealArgs added for that).
- computing reflected Green's tensor (based on Sommerfeld integrals) was split into modules, including the tabulation. Now further optimization efforts can be directed precisely.

Still a lot to do - to test, integrate (add exceptions) to other parts of ADDA, add enhancement rates (radiative and non-radiative) to the output.

Other (related) changes:
- a number of exceptions with respect to combination of different beam types, -prop, and -surf were moved from VariablesInterconnect to InitBeam. Now they are more accurate.
- beam info for Gaussian beam was made more uniform. For centered beams, "Center is in the origin" was changed to "Center position: (0,0,0)".
- new functions cSymMatrVecReal and cReflMatrVecReal in cmplx.h
- version incremented to 1.3b2.
- test suites in tests/2exec/ were updated to include new features.

author: yurkin@gmail.com <yurkin@gmail.com@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
Finally, a working implementation of particle near surface in FFT mode.
- additional required memory was described in comments in calculator.c
- definition of ZsumShift is now different for sparse and FFT modes in parallel (relative to the local or global bottom dipoles respectively). Related difference is in definition of local_Nz_Rm (used for Sommerfeld table and, in FFT mode, for filling Rmatrix).
- Sommerfeld table is now not calculated during prognosis, but corresponding memory is properly accounted for.
- Current implementation requires additional forward fftY and fftZ at each iteration (but see issue 177).
- BlockTranspose_Dm in comm.c was renamed into BlockTranspose_DRm, since it works both for D- and Rmatrix.
- existing functions to index Dmatrix has been slightly changed to not use DsizeYZ and use y>=DsizeY instead of y>smallY.
- functions and plans, not specific to Dmatrix were renamed (Y and Z forward transforms), now they have 'slice' in their names.
- transposeYZ_Dm was changed to transpose (a general function), and transposeYZ is now just a wrapper around the latter.
- version incremented to 1.3b1.

Main computational bottleneck is computation of the table of Sommerfeld integrals. Currently it is approximately equivalent to 200 iterations (issue 176). So should not be a problem for applications with a larger number of iterations.

New implementation was extensively tested against previous sparse version. Still, quantitative comparison with published literature data is required. Remaining limitation is that it doesn't work in OpenCL mode (see issue 101 for details, explicit exception was added to param.c).

Changes to timing:
- added time for 'init interaction' (significant when Sommerfeld table is calculated).
- Time for 'init Dmatrix' now may include the time for initialization of Rmatrix (doesn't include time for Sommerfeld table).
- Precise timing for Dmatrix now includes a separate line for initialization of Rmatrix (without details)

Other:
- scattering at exactly 90 degrees (along surface) for non-trivial surfaces is now handled by a special case to produce exact 0. This makes the output consistent, avoiding large integration errors for -phi_integr or alldir.
- added explicit exception to forbid combination of -no_reduced_fft and -iter cgnr in MPI FFT mode (issue 174).

Tests in tests/2exec/ have been significantly improved
- added SURF_EXT flag, which allows running a large suite of tests, adding '-surf ...' option to each of them.
- added a number of ignores, which are always active (decreases false-positives)
- added a couple of macros in suite files (NOMPI and NOMPISEQ), which indicates that the line should be skipped for a specific comparison modes.
- added a number of tests to the default suite: '-surf ...', '-int_surf', -scat_plane, '-shape read ... -grid ...', '-no_reduced_fft -iter cgnr' (see above)

author: yurkin <yurkin@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
Improvements to the near_field package.

1) Issue 123 describes the inconsistency between ADDA and near_field. ADDA's issue was corrected by r1008, but there still exist some non-trivial functionality in ADDA which can lead to weird shape files. near_field's issue (when working with weird shape files) can be partly alleviated by simple suggestion given by Fabio http://groups.google.com/group/adda-discuss/msg/a1110e72866576fd . 

However, the limitation of it is the assumption that center of the particle coincides (within shift of 0.5 dipoles) with the center of the computational domain. Moreover, two variable (rc{x,y,z} and ic{x,y,z}) are used to describe almost the same quantity, while difference between them is used as an indicator of parity of number of dipoles along the corresponding axes.

The correction sets rc equal to exact center of the computational domain, using both target (integer coordinates) and DipPol (real dipole coordinates). Thus rc is further directly used in e.g. calcbeam to get real coordinates of any point. ic was replaced by pc, which is double the coordinates of the particle center, i.e. the center of the _minimal_ box (with possibly odd sizes) enclosing the particle. Since this center is either integer or half-integer, pc is always integer, which is convenient for further use.

The new version of near_field should work with any shape files, even those not-completely-correct produced by older ADDA versions. This was checked on data provided at http://code.google.com/p/a-dda/issues/detail?id=123#c8 (with small modifications).

2) One of the ways to produce weird shape files, for which the above correction is necessary, is to run ADDA with "-shape read ... grid ..." where arguments to grid are larger than coordinates sizes given by the shape file. Thus a test case was added to RUNTESTS/readodd, which should not be passed by previous version of near_field.

3) All 'run...' scripts were improved by adding checking of ADDA errors. So now the test will not continue if ADDA fails. Also added 'clean' scripts to remove all files produced during runs.

author: yurkin@gmail.com <yurkin@gmail.com@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
Added rigorous calculations of Sommerfeld integrals. Imported somnec.c from NEC2C, which computes the integrals themselves. The remaining code is in interaction.c - it creates a table of integrals (for different rho and z) and further indexes it to calculate the reflected Green's tensor. There is a lot that can be improved, but in sparse mode it has the main functionality associated with substrate. Moreover, the '-int_surf som' is only marginally (10-20%) slower than the '-int_surf img'.

Small comparison of simulation results of a sphere on the surface was performed to compare with (Loke&Menguc,2010) - Figs.10,11. Qualitatively the results are very similar, but there are certain quantitative differences. We will do a more careful benchmarking with the FFT version

Options '-surf <mre> <mim> <h>' was changed to '-surf <h> {<mre> <mim>|inf}'. So the order of parameters has been changed and option to specify perfectly reflecting substrate is now available. The results of '-surf ... inf' were checked to correspond to the limit of increasing <mre> to very large values. For perfectly reflecting substrate the default (and only) method to calculate reflected Green's tensor ('-int surf ...') is the image-dipole one.

Version incremented to 1.3a2. Fixed minor bug in sparse_ops.h, introduced recently. Added function sizetVector to memory.c/h. Call to imExp in CalcReflTerm_img was replaced by accImExp.

Extending the feature introduced in the previous revision, this one adds automatic tracing of the command lines used to compile different classes (C, Fortran, and executables). Another change is that common parts of specific Makefiles was moved to a separate file common.mk that is included from each of the former. This common file is responsible for processing both dependencies and .*opts files.

Also, most of variable assignments in makefiles were changed to immediate ":=", thus it is easier to keep track of their values, especially in the main Makefile.

author: yurkin <yurkin@gmail.com>
commit message:
A lot of improvements to sparse mode:
- Macro (flag) ADDA_SPARSE was shortened to SPARSE.
- Makefiles modified to produce info about SPARSE and USE_SSE3 and set up interaction (errors) with other options.
- Gather operations of sparse mode are now performed through AllGather(). For that it was modified to enable in-place operation, and a new MPI_Datatype mpi_int3 was introduced. Previously used functions and variables has been removed.
- In sparse mode local_nvoid_d0 and local_nvoid_d1 are now initialized in ParSetup(), while SetupLocalD() is not called at all.
- Memory optimizations: material_full and remnants of DipoleCoord_full are eliminated, 'position' is no more allocated but just points to a part of position_full.
- A lot of indexes in sparse_ops.h are now size_t instead of int. Among other changes, Fixes issue 159.
- Fixed initialization of mat_count in MakeParticle() in sparse mode. It was broken and led 
- Timings for init Dmatrix and FFT setup are no more shown in sparse mode.
- All command line options, not supported in sparse mode, are now explicitly removed during compilation (with appropriate modification of help texts). These includes: '-shape ...' (except read), '-init_field wkb', -granul, -save_geom, -sg_format, -store_grans.
- Removed error messages when using '-int ...' (except poi) in sparse mode. Now these options work fine, but relatively slow.
- Information about compile options SPARSE and USE_SSE3 (when used) has been added to output of option -V. Added information about sparse mode to log file (instead of information about FFT method).
- Added meaningful error message for default run of adda (without command line parameters) in sparse mode.
- A lot of formatting changes to make the sparse mode similar to the rest of the code.

Other changes:
- interaction.c/h now holds all the code related to calculation of Green's tensor. In particular, reading/freeing of table integrals was moved from calculator.c, and duplicating code to compute Green's tensor in fft.c was removed. 
An important change is that now functions, which compute Green's tensor do not test for zero argument. Hence, these test is now made in InitDmatrix().
- Intermediate vector DipoleCoord_tmp is no more used in make_particle.c. This somewhat decreases memory usage during prognosis. Overall, the code in MakeParticle() was significantly changed (a lot of moving parts around).
- oclcore.h is now always included, but is void if OPENCL is not specified. That is similar to other conditional headers like fft.h.
- Tests (tests/2exec) were modified to incorporate sparse mode (to compare two sparse mode versions or sparse mode vs. FFT mode). Corresponding tests are listed in separate file - suite_sparse, which is automatically used if appropriate flag is uncommented in comp2exec.  Added 2 new shape files and modified ellipsoid.geom. Improved behavior of diff_numeric.awk - before it was skipping differences, if the line was missing in the first file.
- A number of files (new or heavily modified) were formatted for a window width of 120 symbols.
- A number of minor syntax changes to remove warnings by Eclipse code analyzer. In particular, changed several empty statements from ";" to "{}", removed two unused functions, and hid several extern declarations in sparse mode.
- Fixed crashes when using command line options '-shape' and '-beam' without arguments. Now meaningful error messages are produced.
- version incremented to 1.2b2.

The updated code was tested to compile in different compilation modes (almost all possible combinations) and tested by tests/2exec/ against the version 1.1.

author: yurkin <yurkin@gmail.com>
commit message:
New order of headers in all source files is:
- const.h (see below)
- corresponding header (*.c->*.h)
- project headers
- 3rd party headers
- system headers
Order inside groups is alphabetical. This is more reliable for development (e.g. sefl-sufficiency of corresponding headers is tested automatically during compilation).
The only out-of-way header is const.h, which is now included always in the first place. This is because it contains definition of macro __USE_MINGW_ANSI_STDIO, which tells MinGW64 to use c99-compliant printf-family functions. This macro should be defined before any of the system headers. Overall, this fixes issue with %z format specifiers for 64bit Windows.

Major bug in Makefile was fixed. It was using CPATH variable for communicating with child Makefiles. The side effect is that gcc was adding the project file to search path of system headers. Thus project headers were included instead system ones in certain cases (e.g. io.h). This was causing errors in compilation of C++ files, and warnings during compilation of ADDAmain.c on MinGW64. But more hidden effects could be possible. Overall, we should be more careful in variable naming inside the main Makefile (since they are exported).

author: yurkin <yurkin@gmail.com>
commit message:
First step towards DDA with particles above surface. Currently, mostly infrastructure parts have been handled. The only limitation of the scattering problem is that the particle is located fully above the surface and the upper medium is vacuum (the lower has any complex refractive index). Also, -orient, non-plane waves, -init_field wkb, and radiation forces are currently incompatible with surface.

Implemented:
- command line options '-surf ...', '-int_surf ...' and -scat_plane. The latter defines that the scattering should be calculate in the scattering plane, which passes through prop and ez (in laboratory frame). Two difference from the default behavior (-yz): for default prop, it is the xz-plane, and for non-default prop, the angle is counted from ez, not from prop.
- new definitions of scattered angle as -scat_plane for default calculation, and with respect to the laboratory (surface) reference frame for scat_grid and alldir. Such new definitions are now used only for surface, but may become universal ones in the future (issue 170). 
- incident beam due to surface both for propagation from above and from below surface, including evanescent fields and other complex waves.

Still to do:
- Calculation of scattered fields in the presence of surface (simple reflection and transmission).
- Actually plugging in the surface-interaction Green's tensor, both rigorous (Sommerfeld integrals) and approximate (image dipole) ones
- FFT acceleration of surface mode

Also done:
- A few macros were implemented to specify all components of a real or complex vector (or both real and imaginary parts of the complex number) at once in printf-family arguments.
- Special test mode was added to tests/2exec to test new version with trivial surface (of refractive index 1) against the standard implementation. Also added a combination of -orient -prop, and -scat_matr both to all tests. Improved handling of diffs in IncBeam files.
- Several functions have been added to cmplx.h. In particular, s few memcpy calls were replaced by vCopy.
- Handling of scattering directions based on angles theta and phi (alldir and scat_grid) was localized to a separate function SetScatPlane in crosssec.c. Currently, it contains rather complicated logic to handle differences with surface and all special cases.

The following tests were performed:
- In the default mode no changes with the previous version - tested by tests/2exec (including the new surf_standard test mode, where applicable)
- Use of -scat_plane is equivalent to -store_scat_grid with (phi: type=values, values=90)
- The above equivalence also holds for non-trivial -prop with corresponding shift of theta range. For example, -prop 1 0 1 can be compensated by (theta: min=-45, max=315, and double value of N) in scat_params.dat
- When using non-trivial prop with alldir and trivial -surf (like '-surf 1 0 10'), Csca is the same, while g and Csca.g are rotated from beam RF to laboratory RF.
- When using the non-trivial surface the calculation of incident field was tested (both by -store_beam and by comparing calculated Cext, which is supposed to scale accordingly, since other effects of surface are not yet implemented).

author: yurkin <yurkin@45a4d0da-b139-11dd-ba98-ad202adc45ad>
commit message:
Large edits throughout the code to use C99 features (fixes issue 64), including:
- 'restrict' keyword
- %zu printf format specifiers to directly print out size_t variables. It is already supported by MinGW for printf- in contrast to scanf-family functions.
- use of snprintf and vsnprintf, by implementing their wrappers (SnprintfError, etc.). This should make string processing even more secure. In particular, mismatch of some buffer sizes (defined in const.h) should result in some meaningful error.
- replaced explicit function names by __func__ macro in calls to MultOverflow and CheckOverflow.

Warning settings for the compiler was tightened (now it watches for unused and uninitialized variables). Corresponding changes were made in the code to suppress "legitimate" warnings.
- added 'unused' attribute to some function parameters.
- simplified tests for different enums. Now the last test is made the default one (so that no if is present). Thus the compiler better understands the data flow and do not complain about uninitialized variables.
- LogError function was replaced by two wrappers: LogError and LogWarning, while the main code was moved to ProcessError. Now LogError has attribute 'noreturn', which removes a lot of 'uninitialized' warnings.
- when all of the above didn't help to remove uninitialized warnings, redundant initialization were added to the beginning of a function. The most common case is when variable is initialized inside if and used inside equivalent if later on (for some reason gcc fails to understand this data flow).

- minor change in CatNFiles to actually use input parameter 'dir' instead of default 'directory'. However, this doesn't affect any current calls to this function.

Other changes:
- small parts of granule generator were rewritten and simplified. Also fixes issue 108 and fixes issue 109.
- fixes issue 110 in iterative.c.
- optimization of linalg.c by explicit mentioning of register variables. However, this doesn't seem to help.
- variable 'line' in several places of make_particle.c was changed to size_t type (to potentially allow processing of huge files on 64-bit systems).
- code for reading of ddscat-format shape files was slightly optimized, not to scan dumb variables.
- attribute 'pure' was removed from a few functions, since they change the value of their timing parameter.
- calls to fflush when working with stdout and log were removed. Persistent flushing is maintained only for debug and error/warning messages.
- macros like PRINTZ were replaced by explicit code 'if (IFROOT) printf...', but a shortcut IFROOT - ringid==ADDA_ROOT was introduced. Now the structure of the code is not confused by the macros.

author: yurkin <yurkin@gmail.com>
commit message:
- Calculation of scattering into the substrate was rewritten, using the reciprocity principle. In particular, the near-field propagation direction nN can now be complex. but the far-field wave is now always homogeneous. Fixes issue 184. Now Cext=Csca for dielectric substrate with good accuracy (depends on number of angles to integrate Csca, which is generally larger than for free-space case due to discontinuity at theta=90 deg).
- Scattered field (amplitude) is normalized by k_sca (which is msub times larger, when scattering into the substrate).
- Changed the normalization of the incident beam (when coming from the substrate). Now it has unity amplitude, so that the amplitude matrix directly corresponds to the incident field. New global variable inc_scale=1/Re(minc) is initialized in GenerateB.c (minc is the refractive index of the medium, where the incident beam comes from).
- Muller matrix definition is updated to correspond to ratios of irradiances, so ComputeMuellerMatrix() now includes a factor Re(m_sca)/Re(m_inc) (when needed) and requires theta as additional argument. 
- 'E2_alldir' now stores values scaled with Re(1/msca). This is proportional to the Poynting vector and is more convenient for calculation of Csca and related quantities.
- Cross sections (Cext, Cabs, Csca) and asymmetry vector (g*Csca) are normalized by incoming irradiance, so they now include a factor of inc_scale. Generalization of g to the surface case is straightforward, but loses physical sense (scattered momentum).
- New definition for fields and other computed quantities are given in the manual (will be committed later).
- TestBelowDeg() was added in cmplx.h. imExp_arr() now accepts complex arguments.

Two minor bugs were fixed:
- Detection of symmetry of theta angle (range pi or 2*pi) is improved to correctly account for both -yz and -scat_plane.
- In calculation of scattering plane for SCAT_GRID in MuellerMatrix() theta was used without conversion to radians. But this should not have affected any results.

commit message:
- part of the precise timing definitions was moved to timing.c/h to be available always, as alternative to time(). In particular, it is used for precise measurement of total wall time for program execution. GetTime is replaced by GET_SYSTEM_TIME, DiffSec - by DiffSystemTime.
- minor fixes in precise timing of D-matrix initialization (several printfs were not accounted for, except in total time). Now the total time (for D-matrix init) exactly (within 1 in the last shown digit) equals the sum of the parts. Same is true for other parts of precise timing.
- removed "naive" transpose OpenCL kernels completely, since the cached one works well in all cases.
- rearranged first lines (definitions) in kernels arith2-4, so that they are ordered by arguments of get_global_id/size. This way it is easier to compare those definitions with the arguments of corresponding kernel invocations.
- fftw plans for D,R-matrix transforms (during initialization) are now also destroyed in OpenCL mode. fftw_cleanup calls added in the end of fftw usage (either in fftInitAfterD or in Free_FFT_Dmat).
- minor change in initialization of random generator in PlaceGranules() in make_particle.c. Should not change anything.
- a few cosmetic changes in somnec.c to remove compiler warnings with regards to definition of complex numbers (probably appeared in gcc 4.8).
- r1349 was incorporated (updated) into the code just before the commit. It merged well, so no problems are expected.
